name: Hair bangs / frame hairstyle for eyes

card.summary: Fringe and face-framing hair used to draw attention to the eyes and brow area; a styling choice with little formal research behind the claims.
card.note: Evidence is limited to a cosmetology paper pairing hairlines with fringe styles.

quick.overview:
Bangs (fringe in British usage) are hair that falls over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows. In looksmaxxing discussions, bangs and face-framing styles are said to focus attention on the eye and brow area and to alter the apparent forehead and face shape.

Bangs have a long history across cultures and fashions. Formal research on their effect on eye attractiveness is sparse.
quick.mechanism: Hair covering the forehead changes the visible hairline and frames the upper face. Proponents say this shifts attention to the eyes and shortens a long forehead. A 2022 cosmetology paper cited by Wikipedia paired five hairline shapes with fringe styles.
quick.risks: Styling carries no significant health risks. Practitioners note that bangs need regular trimming and styling.

lead: Bangs, called fringe in British, Australian and New Zealand English, are strands of hair that fall over the front hairline to cover the forehead, usually just above the eyebrows.[1] Their length and shape vary, and modern Western cuts are usually straight, though arc-shaped and ragged versions exist.[1]

In looksmaxxing discussions, bangs and other framing hairstyles are described as a way to draw attention to the eyes and brow area. No published study reviewed for this entry tests that claim directly. A 2022 paper by Park and Jang in the International Journal of Advanced Culture Technology classified five hairline shapes and paired each with a fringe style using wig prototypes, and presents the pairings as cosmetology educational resources.[1]
infobox: Over the forehead, around eyebrow level[1]

paras: The Park and Jang study paired round hairlines with choppy bangs, heart-shaped hairlines with heart bangs, angular hairlines with feather bangs, triangular hairlines with blunt bangs, and flat hairlines with see-through bangs. Wikipedia notes the authors developed these pairings as educational material.[1]

Wikipedia reports that men and women wore bangs in ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome, that they fell out of fashion for European women in the Elizabethan era and Renaissance, and that clergy in the 1600s warned against them as vanity.[1] Curled bangs returned in the Victorian era, including the Alexandra fringe of the 1880s, and in the late 19th and early 20th centuries young immigrant women in the US wore bangs to hide blemishes such as smallpox scars and acne.[1] British bands led by the Beatles from about 1963 popularised bangs among men, a thick blunt-cut fringe revival took place around 2007, and curtain bangs resurged in the 2020s partly through TikTok.[1]

timeline.event: The Alexandra fringe becomes popular in Victorian fashion.[1]
British bands led by the Beatles begin popularising bangs among men.[1]
A revival of thick blunt-cut bangs begins.[1]
Curtain bangs resurge, partly through TikTok.[1]
